note: SIM-GATE-01 (owner, 2026-10-24; amendment of the same day): the one definition of the flight recorder's analysis workbook, read by the GDScript builder (scripts/recorder_export/workbook_builder.gd: the CI gate workbook and the desktop game's live export) and by the Python validator (tools/check_workbook.py). Desktop and CI only: excluded from the Android export (export_presets.cfg). The groupings below are reading aids for the analysis, never game rules; a stat key is matched by its prefix, the first group that matches wins.
runs_note: For a recorded run every value from alive_end on (except wall_seconds) is read from its flight recorder archive by the workbook builder (the closing snapshot in session.json; newcomers counts newcomers, outlaws, arrivals and people returning from a settlement); tools/check_workbook.py compares them with the simulation's own output (economy_sim.gd --out). For a run without the recorder they come from that output.

activity_classes.note: A villager's hourly 'doing' text (sample table) sorted into a class by the first pattern it contains (no text at all is idle); anything else is work. An approximation: the game's own words, read as text.

proposed.note: Values the gate measures and reports but does not block on: no approved requirement sets a number. Each is shown as PROPOSED for the owner, with the value measured in this run.
proposed.stuck_note: A villager counts as stuck when their hourly sample shows them on the same cell, travelling (going, taking, carrying ...) or lost, for this many hours in a row: a walk of three game hours that never leaves its cell. Work, rest and waiting on one cell are normal and not counted.
